title: Replit
summary: An app-building workflow to assess together with its operating costs.

sources.title: Replit Pro Is Here — and Core Now Offers Even Better Value

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: Replit's privacy policy says its Services are primarily hosted in the United States and may also be hosted elsewhere; using the Services can transfer data to the United States and other hosting jurisdictions. This does not identify every project resource or an account's geography settings.

facts.label: Product self-hosting
facts.value: Replit's current Enterprise page lists a dedicated GCP project and a single-tenant option under Sales-Assisted Enterprise, with custom pricing and an annual commitment. The page does not state who owns or operates the project or which components it includes, so it does not establish a customer-operated or self-hosted Replit platform. No account, agreement or deployment was inspected.

facts.label: Code / data portability
facts.value: Replit documents Git/GitHub connectivity and an App-managed gitsafe-backup remote that can restore the App's Git commit history after its local repository is corrupted. Its import guide lists GitHub, Bitbucket and ZIP plus named builder sources; source-specific settings, secrets, database values or services may need separate setup. One documented provider-import path says existing Supabase records and secrets are not imported. Agent checkpoints are an in-platform rollback path covering project state and AI context, with development database restoration optional; production database restore is not automatic. These documents cover code/repository recovery and platform-local rollback, not a tested full external app export or migration.

facts.label: Published app geography
facts.value: Replit documents publishing-region selection for Core, Pro and Enterprise across North America, Europe (EU), Asia, South America and Australia; Free customers publish to North America by default. Published compute, database and Object Storage are colocated. The choice cannot be changed after publishing, and pre-publish resources may remain elsewhere.

facts.label: Development workspace geography
facts.value: Workspace geography is separate from publishing geography, is selected when a workspace is created, is available only on Pro and cannot be changed later. The workspace and published app regions do not need to match.

facts.label: Agent model routing and app AI integrations
facts.value: Replit AI Integrations let Agent set up application API calls with Replit-managed provider credentials, billed at provider API prices through Replit credits, or a developer's own provider API key billed directly by that provider. Replit's Aug 2026 Intelligent Model Routing announcement says it selects a model per task; all users start in Free Mode and are notified when work escalates to higher-powered modes that can incur usage costs, with an option to remain in Free Mode. Core and Pro users can manually select models, while Enterprise administrators can define the approved model set. The reviewed sources do not say where routed models run or establish a local inference endpoint for Agent; local-model support remains unknown.

prices.name: Replit Core (annual billing equivalent)
prices.billing: The public pricing page displays USD 18/month billed annually, discounted from USD 20/month. This is a base-plan equivalent, not a regional checkout quote.
prices.allowance: USD 20 toward the most powerful models per month; does not represent the full app operating budget.

prices.name: Replit Core (monthly billing)
prices.billing: Replit's pricing announcement updated 2026-09-15 lists Core at USD 20/month; the pricing page also offers annual billing with up to 10% off. Regional checkout may differ.
prices.allowance: USD 20 toward the most powerful models per month; does not represent the full app operating budget.

sections.heading: Budget building and running
paragraphs: Replit's current sources list Core at USD 20/month and USD 18/month equivalent on annual billing. Record the applicable billing period, location-dependent taxes and checkout amount; neither base price is a full application budget.

sections.heading: Trial operational changes
paragraphs: After the first successful demo, change a data field and repair a deliberately failing request. Rehearse recovery with synthetic data. Record how code, data and configuration would be recovered outside the original workflow.

pros.text: Replit describes Agent as a plain-language workflow that plans, creates applications, checks its work, fixes problems and deploys.
Agent checkpoints can capture project files, conversation context and connected database state for rollback inside Replit.

cons.text: A checkpoint is a Replit recovery feature; it does not establish an independently tested export or recovery path outside the platform.
The public Core base prices are USD 20/month with monthly billing and USD 18/month equivalent on annual billing; runtime, database and agent usage remain separate budget items.

faqs.question: What does Replit Agent do?
faqs.answer: Replit says Agent can take a plain-language idea through project setup, app creation, checking, problem fixing and deployment; validate the result for your own workload.

faqs.question: Do Replit's model-routing and AI integration pages establish local-model support for Agent?
faqs.answer: Replit's Aug 2026 Intelligent Model Routing announcement says Replit selects models per task; all users start in Free Mode and are notified when work escalates to higher-powered modes that can incur usage costs, with an option to remain in Free Mode. Core and Pro users can manually select models, and Enterprise administrators can define the approved model set. AI Integrations separately describes provider API calls for apps being built, while the Model selector describes choices for Replit Agent. These sources do not say where routed models run or establish a local inference endpoint, so local-model support remains unverified rather than being marked unsupported. No account, endpoint, integration or model was tested.

faqs.question: Do Replit's backup and import docs establish a complete external migration?
faqs.answer: No. Replit documents Git repository backup and imports from GitHub, Bitbucket and ZIP, while provider-specific data, secrets and services may need separate setup. Agent checkpoints support rollback inside Replit; production database restore is not automatic. Inventory the exact app resources and test an independent deployment. No export, import or restore was tested.

faqs.question: What Replit Core prices are publicly listed?
faqs.answer: Replit's current sources list USD 20/month with monthly billing and USD 18/month equivalent when billed annually. Taxes depend on location; confirm your exact checkout and budget runtime, database and agent usage separately.

faqs.question: Does Replit Enterprise offer customer-hosted Replit?
faqs.answer: Replit's Sales-Assisted Enterprise page lists a dedicated GCP project and a single-tenant option under custom pricing with an annual commitment. It does not specify who owns or operates the project or whether the Replit platform is customer-managed, so this does not establish self-hosting. Confirm architecture, terms and app/resource scope with Replit; no account or deployment was checked.

verdict: Evaluate the full build-to-operation loop, not just the first demo. Require a separate estimate for editing and the live application.
bestFor: Builders comparing a hosted development workflow
notFor: Projects with an unverified residency or private-network requirement
migration: Use Replit's documented Git/import paths for code, then inventory environment secrets, database records, production data, domains and provider-specific services separately. Rehearse an independent build and restore before considering a migration complete; no migration was tested.
gaps: Confirm current account eligibility, location-based taxes and total application costs; public Core base prices are not a regional checkout quote or full operating budget.

Confirm whether the documented workspace and publishing geography settings meet the proposed residency requirement across pre-existing storage, other platform resources and connected services; no account or deployment was checked, and published-region selection is permanent.
Review the applicable data-processing terms for the intended use; the general privacy policy is not an account-specific service-location map or a legal review.

The reviewed docs cover Git-repository recovery, selected source imports and in-platform checkpoints, not a verified full export outside Replit. Confirm the required secrets, database records, production data, domains, deployment settings and connected services; no export, import, restore or independent deploy was tested.

The reviewed AI Integrations and Agent Model selector docs distinguish application provider API calls from Agent model selection but do not establish local-model inference for Replit Agent. Confirm the required local endpoint capability; no account, model, integration or endpoint was tested.

Clarify who owns and operates the dedicated GCP project, which Replit components it includes, and whether a customer-managed platform deployment is available. The Enterprise page lists a single-tenant option but does not define those boundaries; no account, agreement or deployment was inspected.
